about: What kind of place a page is on, and so how its claims are labelled. PRIMARY is the company speaking for itself: its own website (investor relations, newsroom), its filings (on its site or on EDGAR) and its press releases (on its site or on a wire service that carries them). SECONDARY is anyone reporting on those: publications and databases that cite the filings and releases. A wire service or filing database is primary only when the page is the subject company's own document, so those hosts also need the company's name on the page; otherwise they are secondary. Reference works are for general-purpose knowledge only and are not used for a key development or news about a company.
